A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QRHEAD/QRRETRIEVER research. Text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison; v1 Appendices D-F are retained as v2 Appendices G-I.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval and reasoning experiments, head-selection ablations, generalization analyses and NIAH masking results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results, revises benchmark scores and adds inference-latency and head-count experiments in Appendices E-F.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 retain the same query-context attention scoring, head-selection procedure, null-query calibration and retrieval/generation pipeline. Newly documented prompts and head-count experiments do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongMemEval, CLIPPER, the same 11 BEIR domains, NIAH and the same length-generalization scenarios. The added latency and head-count experiments use NQ, already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding experiments is unchanged, including dense/cross-encoder baselines, RankGPT variants, ICR and head-selection controls. The new latency comparison reuses ICR and RankGPTBubble rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 changes the stated NQ head-detection sample from 128 to 256 held-out examples; this is a reported setting revision, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Appendices E-F add average-latency measurement and head-count sweeps for the existing 8B and 70B models.

E4.justification: Appendix F/Table 8 adds sensitivity to the number of selected heads: 16/64/256 for 8B and 32/128/512 for 70B. Appendix E/Table 7 adds a runtime-performance comparison. Existing head-selection, scoring/data ablations, length generalization, detection-subset stability and NIAH analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 6 retains the same three disjoint 128-example detection subsets and individual results. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the new tables also report point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 substantially revise QRRETRIEVER and ICR results. Table 1 changes 70B LongMemEval ICR Recall@5 from 45.6 to 32.1 and QRRETRIEVER Top-10 accuracy from 63.3 to 67.7. The 8B CLIPPER Top-5 ranking reverses: QRRETRIEVER/ICR changes from 44.4/42.3 to 41.9/42.5. Table 2 replaces BEIR scores alongside the changed detection sample, including the 8B QRRETRIEVER average of 49.7 becoming 50.0; this is not a controlled same-setting gain. Tables 7-8 add latency measurements and head-count results.

T1.justification: The task formulation and Equations 1-5 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised; QRScore capitalization edits do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about query-focused heads, improved long-context reasoning, zero-shot re-ranking and generalization. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets degradation from including more heads as supporting retrieval-head sparsity. The existing generation-versus-retrieval hypothesis and limitations concerning mechanism understanding, broader tasks, parameter updates and English-only evaluation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents prompt templates for ICR/QRRETRIEVER and RankGPT in Figures 5-6. This improves implementation documentation without establishing that the prompts changed. Code/checkpoint links, hardware disclosures and data-segmentation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds Liu et al. (2024b), Sliding Windows Are Not the End: Exploring Full Ranking with Long-Context Large Language Models, to its efficiency discussion. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized affiliation and terminology corrections, updates result descriptions, adds a short introduction to Section 6 and inserts three appendix sections. The main narrative and section order are largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds two boxed prompt figures and two tables for latency and head-count results. Table 4 moves from PDF page 7 to page 8, with corresponding text and appendix reflow. Existing figure designs and main-table structures remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added prompt templates improve reproducibility, while measured latency and head-count sensitivity better support existing efficiency and selection arguments. Section 5.2 also corrects v1's mixing of LongMemEval recall with CLIPPER accuracy. These are useful, limited gains. Unexplained revisions to primary scores and the changed BEIR detection sample prevent treating numerical increases themselves as evidence of improved paper quality.
